name: Nellie Kim
milestone_by_age_26: Won three gold medals and one silver at the 1976 Montreal Olympics at age 19, scoring perfect 10.0s on vault and floor exercise — the first woman to achieve perfect scores on those apparatuses.
early_history_summary: Born in Shurab, Tajik SSR, to a Sakhalin Korean father and Tatar mother, Kim began gymnastics at age 9 at the Chimkent City Children and Youth Sports School under trainers Vladimir Baidin and Galina Barkova. She compensated for initial lack of flexibility with superior technique and difficulty, placing fifth at the 1971 Junior USSR Championships at 14 and winning bronze on beam at the 1974 World Championships at 17.
family_context_summary: Born to a Sakhalin Korean father, Vladimir Kim, who worked in the Chimkent slate factory, and a Tatar mother, Alfiya Safina, in Shurab, Tajik SSR; the family later moved to Kazakh SSR. Working-class family with no documented gymnastics background.

The Soviet gymnastics pipeline provided elite-level training and competition opportunities through the Spartak Sports Society and national team selection. She compensated for initial lack of flexibility with superior technique and difficulty, progressing from Junior USSR Championships at 14 to World Championships bronze at 17.
